data.content_ref: inline:{"claim": "Two conclusions are the same claim iff they are assigned the same identifier by the system's theory-of-mind module, which models the beliefs of the system's own sub-agents and detects when two conclusions play identical roles in the internal belief dynamics.", "mechanism": "The system maintains a set of internal 'belief states' for each sub-agent. When two conclusions are generated, the system simulates how each would be used by sub-agents in planning and communication; if the resulting belief states are indistinguishable, the conclusions are merged.", "scope": {"covers": ["modular systems with internal agent models"], "excludes": ["monolithic reasoners without self-modeling"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "Two conclusions are indistinguishable in the internal simulation but lead to different external actions when the system interacts with the environment, because the simulation failed to capture a relevant environmental constraint.", "eval": "program:simulation_environment_mismatch"}, {"case": "Two conclusions are treated as distinct by the theory-of-mind module because they were generated by different sub-agents, but they are logically identical and merging would reduce redundancy without harm.", "eval": "program:overcautious_separation"}], "prose_notes": "This criterion risks merging claims that are only contextually identical within the system's self-model but differ in external application, or keeping separate claims that are truly identical but attributed to different internal sources."}
